findings.problem: The completion criteria require that the security pass has run, but Increment F permits the owner to decline it and then ends with no change. In that permitted outcome the plan can never meet its own completion criteria.
findings.suggestion: Make the security review an explicit owner checkpoint and define the declined outcome consistently: either require the review before the plan can complete, or revise the criterion and Result requirements to record the owner’s declined review without claiming the pass ran.

findings.problem: Increment F can deliberately finish with no change and no commit, conflicting with both the plan’s stated one-commit-per-increment constraint and the plan format’s requirement that every increment produces exactly one local commit.
findings.suggestion: Make the security pass a checkpoint rather than an increment when it finds no changes, and reserve an increment for any independently reviewed remediation commit; or specify the required tracked result-record commit for the no-findings/no-review outcome.

summary: The plan otherwise aligns with its named specs and has no roadmap candidate to review, but its conditional security-review path makes completion and increment evidence internally inconsistent.
